evidence.quote: Patients who have submitted a financial assistance application with complete information and who have qualified for financial assistance will receive a 100 percent discount.
Hardship charity, under guidelines established by BayCare, extends beyond AHCA charity limits and includes patients with gross family income up to 250 percent of the federal poverty level.

asset_test.details: Liquid assets over $50,000 for the household may make a patient ineligible; for insured non-Medicare patients, liquid assets exceeding five times the patient responsibility; for uninsured patients, liquid assets exceeding five times total charges. Medicare recipients must provide proof of income and assets.

evidence.quote: If available liquid assets are over $50,000 for the household, the patient may not be eligible for financial assistance.

residency.area: Florida residents / hospital service area; non-Florida residents seeking planned services may not receive assistance

evidence.quote: Non-Florida residents seeking financial assistance while visiting Florida for planned services
Patients may request financial assistance up to one year after the date of service.

presumptive_eligibility: Uninsured emergency room patients within three months of date of service may be presumptively approved via third-party analytics if their reported FPL meets criteria; not for minors under 18.
how_to_apply: Call (855) 233-1555, visit BayCareFinancialAssistance.org, or get applications from hospital Registration areas, emergency rooms, or Financial Assistance offices; return by mail, fax or email per application directions.
warnings: Policy has two programs: AHCA charity (income under 200% FPL, or hospital expenses over 25% of annual family income) and Hardship charity (up to 250% FPL). Qualifying patients receive a 100% discount, but the policy also says patients won't pay more than AGB, so the free-care limit is ambiguous.

Application deadline is ambiguous: policy says 240 days from first post-discharge billing statement for incomplete applications, and also says patients may request assistance up to one year after date of service.

Uninsured patients not qualifying get a 40% discount (plus 10% if paid within 30 days) under a separate Uninsured Patient Discount Policy; this is not financial assistance under this policy and is not listed as a tier.
AHCA criteria also mention total gross family income cannot exceed four times FPL for a family of four, in addition to the 200% criterion.
Asset thresholds vary by patient type and the policy says 'may not be eligible', not a hard rule.
